In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
L-sorbose is used by E. coli by the same route as L-arabinose, and that L-sorbofuranose is used by the same route that E. coli uses D-xylose.
L-sorbose is used in E. coli as a result of the activity of a phosphoenolpyruvate-dependent phosphotransfer system.

L-sorbose is metabolized by E. coli by the Entner-Doudoroff pathway, and the genes for L-sorbosone dehydrogenase and sorbose isomerase are adjacent on the genetic map.
